“Happy to help” is such a reflex — it comes out before you’ve even decided anything. She said “we’re stretched,” and your mouth said the polite thing while the rest of you was still catching up. That’s not you being a pushover in some deep character way. That’s a workplace trained you to smooth things over fast.

But then the week happened. Staying late every night is where the reflex turned into a real cost — your evenings, your energy, and the message it sends: *this is fine, no need to discuss it.* The “happy to help” was one sentence. The late nights are the part that’s still happening.

You don’t have to retroactively un-say it or make a big confession about it. You can just let the next sentence be different. Something like: “I’ve been covering Debbie’s paperwork this week and staying late to keep up. I want to talk about how this gets handled going forward — including pay.” That doesn’t contradict “happy to help.” It just adds the part you left out.

Do you want to figure out the timing — like who to say it to and when — or is the bigger hurdle right now just getting past the cringe of having said yes so easily?
